items.claim: Workday raised FY26 subscription revenue guidance to $8.815 billion, 14% growth, reflecting the Paradox acquisition impact.
items.quote: FY '26 subscription revenue guidance to $8.815 billion
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Zane Rowe gave Q3 FY26 subscription revenue guidance of approximately $2.235 billion, also 14% growth.
items.quote: expect Q3 FY '26 subscription revenue to be approximately
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Zane Rowe guided Q3 cRPO growth of 15%-16%, explicitly excluding the Paradox acquisition impact.
items.quote: We expect cRPO to increase between 15% and 16% in Q3.
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Carl Eschenbach stated Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 29%, alongside 14% subscription revenue growth.
items.quote: non-GAAP operating margin of 29%
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Zane Rowe raised FY26 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to approximately 29%, citing ongoing efficiencies.
items.quote: our FY '26 non-GAAP operating margin to approximately 29%
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Zane Rowe guided Q3 non-GAAP operating margin of 28%, and noted GAAP margins run ~17-21 points lower.
items.quote: For Q3, we expect non-GAAP operating margin of 28%.
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Workday repurchased $299 million of shares during the quarter.
items.quote: repurchased $299 million of our shares during the quarter
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Workday ended the quarter with $8.2 billion in cash and marketable securities.
items.quote: $8.2 billion in cash and marketable securities
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Workday had $1.2 billion in remaining buyback authorization as of July 31.
items.quote: $1.2 billion in remaining authorization as of July 31
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Workday signed a definitive agreement to acquire Paradox, a conversational-AI candidate experience agent, expected to close in Q3.
items.quote: signed a definitive agreement to acquire Paradox
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Carl Eschenbach disclosed Workday also recently acquired Flowise, a low-code platform for building AI agents.
items.quote: we also recently acquired Flowise, a leading low-code
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Workday launched Workday Government as a wholly owned subsidiary dedicated to the U.S. government sector.
items.quote: we launched Workday Government, a wholly owned subsidiary
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Responding to a question about AI-driven SaaS disruption, Carl Eschenbach called the negative impact on seat-based models overblown.
items.quote: impact on seat-based models are completely overblown
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Carl Eschenbach cited winning customers in Germany located near larger competitors' home base as evidence of international competitive strength.
items.quote: right in the backyard of some of our bigger competitors
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Carl Eschenbach acknowledged a headwind in the state and local government portion of the SLED business.
items.quote: we did see a little bit of headwind in that market
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Carl Eschenbach flagged that higher education customers are under funding pressure, including loss of federal funding.
items.quote: higher ed is clearly under pressure
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Despite analyst questions about tariffs and geopolitical cross-currents, Carl Eschenbach said Workday has not seen international macro headwinds this quarter.
items.quote: we haven't necessarily seen any blowback or headwinds
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Carl Eschenbach stated Workday serves more than 65% of the Fortune 500.
items.quote: We are proud to serve more than 65% of the Fortune 500
items.speaker: Carl Eschenbach (CEO)

items.claim: Zane Rowe reported gross revenue retention remained healthy at 97%.
items.quote: gross revenue retention rates remained healthy at 97%.
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Zane Rowe reaffirmed Workday is tracking well against deliverables tied to the previously flagged DIA (Defense Intelligence Agency) contract.
items.quote: talked all year long about the deliverables tied to the DIA
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

items.claim: Zane Rowe said management will host a Financial Analyst Day on September 16 to share the framework for future growth and margin expansion.
items.quote: our upcoming Financial Analyst Day on September 16
items.speaker: Zane Rowe (CFO)

qa_flags.question: Kash Rangan (Goldman Sachs) followed up asking for Carl Eschenbach's viewpoint on Sam Altman/OpenAI's comment about entering SaaS.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Carl Eschenbach did not engage with the substance, saying he had no viewpoint because he did not know what OpenAI meant, then pivoted to a generic line that 'AI is software' rather than addressing the competitive implication raised.

qa_flags.question: Karl Keirstead (UBS) asked Zane Rowe to roughly size the basis-point upside to cRPO from elevated early renewals in the quarter.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Zane Rowe did not give a specific bps figure, instead saying it was 'probably above the range' and that early renewals were 'a big contributor,' avoiding quantification of the specific number requested.

qa_flags.question: Raimo Lenschow (Barclays) pressed Zane Rowe to reconcile the math: a Q2 beat of roughly $9 million plus $15 million from Paradox should imply a larger guidance raise than what was given.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Zane Rowe did not directly reconcile the arithmetic the analyst laid out, instead repeating general reassurance ('a lot that goes into our forecast,' 'we feel great about the year') without addressing the specific dollar gap questioned.
